INSTRUCTION FROM THE HELIUMDEPLOY TEAM. Georges typed this in the team inbox. It is not a message from the customer and the customer cannot see it.
Task: RMA APPROVED by Georges for GekkoScience KBOX on Shop····. Hal's verdict: defective (Hashboard does not come up: zero hashrate on UI and screen with power draw stuck at idle (9-14W), chips never enabled, consistent with a cooked voltage regulator / TPS on the board). Do the rest now, in this order: 1) order-swap skill: return_order.py plan, then create --confirmed (the return reference is the order number plus RMA, the label link comes back); 2) rma_replacement.py create for the same order (the replacement is a $0 order held on both sides until the unit is back with us; it releases by itself when the warehouse receives it. If you OFFER a different unit and wait for their answer, create it with --await-customer, and the moment they say yes run rma_replacement.py confirm --what "<their words>" --confirmed yourself, never leave the yes for the team); 3) tell the customer: the return is approved, here is the prepaid label, write the reference on the box, and the replacement ships as soon as their unit arrives at our warehouse. If any step stops, flag it and tell them the team will confirm the next step by email.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.
